label: Game A
nuance_found: Bloom is worth saving: use it when a crowd gathers and it also opens the inkwell's nodes. Painted ground heals you, so fight on colour. After the first inkwell you pick a lens (Rapid or Arc), a real but one-time choice. Otherwise it is walk, aim at things, hold fire.
audio: Looping music from about 2 s, plus constant shot blips, kill chords and a harsh buzz when hurt; the sound is busy but reads clearly when I score or get hit.
furthest_progress: Broke the first inkwell (Olive Terraces, 1 of 5) at about 322 s, picked Arc lens, walked into Millbrook village and reached the second inkwell once (died there). About 5.5% of the valley restored, score about 130,000, died roughly 12 times.
control_trouble: Two thumbs on a flat screen with a 0.5 s view: camera aim over- and under-shot constantly, the view tilted to the ground or sky, and I walked past the inkwell several times. Some of the dying is mine, but the pink damage arc was hard to read for any thumb.
best_moment: Bloomstorm: colour bursts across the hillside, the score jumps by tens of thousands and the grey valley turns painted and warm.
worst_moment: Dying again and again to things I could not see, then walking 100+ metres back from the lantern each time and losing score.
verdict: The first 30 seconds were bad: I could not see what was hurting me, I died with zero kills and nothing told me to turn around. I would have deleted it there. Then I got a few kills and it changed: the painted ground, the big score numbers and Bloomstorm are very satisfying, and the sketch-to-colour look is lovely on a phone. But I died about a dozen times, mostly to unseen attackers or the guardians at the inkwell, and each death costs a long walk and some score. Clear goals and small wins are what I like, and the inkwell goal is clear once you get it, but the road to the first win took over five minutes. A 5 for me, maybe a 6 if the early game were kinder.
